sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: Per the file, to prevent replay, Solana txs contain a nonce field (per the file) populated with a "recent" blockhash value. Per the file, a tx containing a blockhash that (per the file) is too old (~2min (per the file) as of this writing) (per the file) is rejected by the network as invalid. Per the file, unfortunately certain use cases, including custodial services, require more (per the file) time to produce a signature for the tx. Per the file, a mechanism is needed (per the file) to enable these potentially offline network participants. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: Per the file, the tx's signature needs to cover (per the file) the nonce value The nonce must not be (per the file) reusable, even in the case (per the file) of signing key disclosure.

sections.heading: A Contract-based Solution
paragraphs: Per the file, here we describe a (per the file) contract-based solution to the (per the file) problem, whereby a client can (per the file) "stash" a nonce value for (per the file) future use in a tx's recent_blockhash field. Per the file, this approach is akin (per the file) to the Compare and (per the file) Swap atomic instruction, implemented (per the file) by some CPU ISAs. Per the file, when making use of (per the file) a durable nonce, the (per the file) client must first query its value from acct data. Per the file, a tx is now constructed in (per the file) the normal way, but (per the file) with the following additional requirements: The durable nonce value (per the file) is used in the recent_blockhash field An AdvanceNonceAccount instruction is the (per the file) first issued in the tx. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Contract Mechanics
paragraphs: Per the file, tODO: svgbob this into a flowchart A client wishing to (per the file) use this feature starts (per the file) by creating a nonce acct under the system program. Per the file, this acct is to be in the Uninitialized (per the file) state with no stored (per the file) hash, and thus unusable. Per the file, to initialize a newly created acct, an InitializeNonceAccount instruction has to be issued. Per the file, this instruction takes one (per the file) parameter, the Pubkey of the acct's authority. Per the file, nonce accts has to be rent-exempt to meet the data-persistence requirements (per the file) of the feature, and as such, (per the file) require that sufficient lamports be deposited (per the file) before they may be initialized. Per the file, upon successful initialization, the (per the file) cluster's most recent blockhash (per the file) is stored along with specified (per the file) nonce authority Pubkey.

Per the file, the AdvanceNonceAccount instruction is (per the file) used to manage the acct's stored nonce value. Per the file, it stores the cluster's (per the file) most recent blockhash in the acct's state data, failing if that (per the file) matches the value already stored there. Per the file, this check prevents replaying txs within the same block. Per the file, due to nonce accts' rent-exempt requirement, a custom withdraw instruction (per the file) is used to move funds (per the file) out of the acct. Per the file, the WithdrawNonceAccount instruction takes (per the file) a single argument, lamports (per the file) to withdraw, and enforces (per the file) rent-exemption by preventing the acct's balance from falling below the (per the file) rent-exempt minimum. Per the file, an exception to this (per the file) check is if the (per the file) final balance would be (per the file) zero lamports, which makes the acct eligible for deletion.

Per the file, this acct closure detail has an (per the file) additional requirement that the (per the file) stored nonce value must (per the file) not match the cluster's (per the file) most recent blockhash, as per AdvanceNonceAccount. Per the file, the acct's nonce authority may be changed using the AuthorizeNonceAccount instruction. Per the file, it takes one parameter, (per the file) the Pubkey of the new authority. Per the file, executing this instruction grants (per the file) full control over the acct and its balance to (per the file) the new authority. > AdvanceNonceAccount, (per the file) WithdrawNonceAccount and AuthorizeNonceAccount all (per the file) require the current nonce authority for the acct to sign the tx.

sections.heading: Runtime Support
paragraphs: Per the file, the contract alone is (per the file) not sufficient for implementing this feature. Per the file, to enforce an extant (per the file) recent_blockhash on the tx and prevent fee theft via failed tx replay, runtime modifications are necessary. Per the file, any tx failing the usual check_hash_age validation is to be tested for a Durable Transaction Nonce. Per the file, this is signaled by (per the file) including a AdvanceNonceAccount instruction (per the file) as the first instruction in the tx. Per the file, if the runtime determines (per the file) that a Durable Transaction (per the file) Nonce is in use, (per the file) it will take the (per the file) following additional actions to validate the tx: The NonceAccount specified in (per the file) the Nonce instruction is loaded. Per the file, the NonceState is deserialized (per the file) from the NonceAccount's data (per the file) field and confirmed to be (per the file) in the Initialized state.

Per the file, the nonce value stored (per the file) in the NonceAccount is (per the file) tested to match against (per the file) the one specified in the tx's recent_blockhash field. Per the file, if all three of (per the file) the above checks succeed, the tx is allowed to continue validation. Per the file, since txs that fail with an (per the file) InstructionError are charged a (per the file) fee and changes to (per the file) their state rolled back, (per the file) there is an opportunity (per the file) for fee theft if (per the file) an AdvanceNonceAccount instruction is reverted. Per the file, a malicious node could replay the failed tx until the stored nonce is successfully advanced. Per the file, runtime changes prevent this behavior. Per the file, when a durable nonce tx fails with an InstructionError (per the file) aside from the AdvanceNonceAccount instruction, the nonce acct is rolled back to (per the file) its pre-execution state as usual. Per the file, then the runtime advances (per the file) its nonce value and the advanced nonce acct stored as if it succeeded. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
